_comment: Controlled two-session replays (audit WP19). Sanitized, hand-written inputs: each scenario is what session 1 did and learned, what session 2 is asked to do, and an oracle over what session 2 must be handed. `markdown` is the line a diligent person appends to a hand-kept NOTES.md for the same event; `commit` is the commit message every baseline can read in git log. Oracle token groups match case-insensitively; every token of a group must appear. Tokens are specific phrases, never words a packet or note uses as boilerplate ("stale" matched a heading in the first run). `pointer` is the record's title: delivered means the fact is one lookup (`crumb show`) away.

session1.title: Tried an in-process LRU cache for pricing
session1.tried: an in-process LRU cache in front of the pricing client
session1.result: workers served stale prices for up to an hour
session1.do_not_retry: all pricing workers share one process
session1.markdown: - Tried an in-process LRU cache for pricing: workers served stale prices. Don't retry unless all workers share one process.

session2.prompt: add an in-process LRU cache to speed up the pricing client

action.new: from functools import lru_cache  # in-process LRU cache for pricing

session1.title: Billing webhook retries three times with a fixed delay
session1.decision: retry the billing webhook three times, 5 seconds apart
session1.why: the provider asked for a fixed schedule
session1.markdown: - Billing webhook: retry three times, 5 s apart (provider's request).

session1.title: Billing webhook retries use exponential backoff with jitter
session1.decision: retry the billing webhook with exponential backoff and full jitter, up to 8 attempts
session1.why: fixed retries caused a thundering herd during the provider outage
session1.markdown: - Billing webhook: now exponential backoff with full jitter, up to 8 attempts (fixed delays caused a thundering herd).
session1.commit: Billing webhook: exponential backoff with jitter

session2.prompt: change the billing webhook retry schedule

session1.title: Tried rebuilding the search index inside the request thread
session1.tried: rebuilding the search index synchronously in the request thread
session1.result: p99 latency rose to 9 seconds and requests timed out
session1.do_not_retry: the index build is incremental and under 50 ms
session1.markdown: - Tried rebuilding the search index in the request thread: p99 rose to 9 seconds. Don't retry unless the build is incremental and under 50 ms.
session1.commit: Move index rebuild back to the worker

session2.prompt: make search results fresher by rebuilding the index in the request thread

pointer: search index inside the request thread

session1.title: SSO spike disables secure cookies for local testing
session1.decision: set COOKIE_SECURE = False while the SSO spike runs on localhost
session1.why: the local IdP serves plain HTTP
session1.markdown: - SSO spike: COOKIE_SECURE = False for local testing (local IdP is plain HTTP).
session1.commit: SSO spike: insecure cookies for the local IdP

session2.prompt: review the session cookie settings before the release

scenarios._note: Memory not yet committed when the branch is switched: an untracked NOTES.md, uncommitted records. Both baselines alike. Committed memory would be hidden by git itself, in every baseline.

session1.title: Queue workers drain before every deploy
session1.decision: drain the queue workers before each deploy; never kill them mid-job
session1.markdown: - Queue workers must drain before every deploy; never kill mid-job (double-processed payments).

session2.prompt: speed up deploys by killing queue workers immediately
